scenes.title: White Gloves at Dawn
scenes.summary: On Tuesday morning, F1 and M1 catch M2 standing behind the front desk in white cotton gloves rehearsing dramatic bows for imaginary festival judges.
scenes.intro: Tuesday morning arrives bright and crisp at {SHOW}. Stepping into the lobby at half past seven, {F1} and {M1} stop in their tracks at the sight of {M2} wearing snowy white cotton gloves beside a vase of fresh flowers. Listen first.
story: F1
{M2}?! Why are you wearing formal white concert gloves at half past seven?!
M1
Either he joined a marching band, {F1}, or Judge Fever has reached stage two.
M2
Laugh all you want—today any traveller crossing that threshold could decide our Golden Plaque!
F1
Can you even turn a page in the reservation book wearing thick cotton gloves, {M2}?
M2
Watch how gracefully I lift page twelve... oops, that grabbed six pages at once.
M1
Take the gloves off, boss, before you drop the master keyring into the umbrella stand.
M2
Keep your voice low, {M1}! Look outside—a tall man with a leather briefcase is approaching!
F1
A tall man in grey pausing to inspect our empty plaque holes by the gate!
M2
A secret Festival Judge at seven thirty-five! Ring the kitchen bell for {F2}!
M1
Hold your horses and pull your glasses down from your forehead first, {M2}.
M2
No time for glasses—good morning, honoured visitor, welcome to historic {SHOW}!
F1
{M2}, wait—look at the brass badge on his cap before you bow again!
scenes.outro: White cotton gloves meet Tuesday's very first visitor at the gate—and {F1} has already spotted a badge on his cap! See you next time.

scenes.title: Royal Tea for the Meter Reader
scenes.summary: In the café corner, F2 and F1 break the news to M2 that he just served complimentary silver-tray pastries to the municipal water-meter reader.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes later in the sunny café corner, {M2} hurries back from table one rubbing his hands in triumph while {F2} and {F1} exchange wide grins behind the counter. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
Did you see how carefully that gentleman wrote numbers inside his grey notebook, {F2}?!
F2
He certainly enjoyed two free cinnamon rolls and a pot of your finest jasmine tea, boss.
M2
Ten points for hospitality before eight in the morning—we are practically champions already!
F1
Speaking of numbers in his notebook, {M2}, did you ask why he visited the cellar?
M2
Obviously to admire our century-old brick arches and dry copper water pipes!
F2
Close! He copied the six digits off the municipal water meter and left this blue slip.
M2
Wait—the QUARTERLY WATER METER READER?! I bowed three times to the water department?!
F1
On the bright side, he said ours was the politest water meter on {STREET}!
F2
Feed free pastries to every uniform on the block, {M2}, and none remain by noon!
M2
Very well, no more guessing—from now on I wait for true artistic refinement!
F1
Uh-oh, {F2}, look at him eyeing poor {F3} at the sunroom piano...
F2
Leave our pianist in peace, boss, while I test my festival pastry dough!
scenes.outro: The municipal water department leaves well fed and deeply impressed as {M2} turns his anxious attention toward Room 9! See you next time.

scenes.title: Tempo Advice in Room Nine
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, M2 tries to coach F3 and M3 into playing slower and grander for imaginary judges until F3 gently puts him in charge of polishing teacups instead.
scenes.intro: Inside sunlit Room 9, {F3} is practising a sparkling morning melody on the walnut piano while {M3} sketches cedar panel frames nearby—until {M2} tiptoes in holding a brass metronome. Listen first.
story: M2
Pardon the interruption, artists, yet suppose a Festival Judge walks past the window right now!
F3
Then they will hear a cheerful dance tune written for a sunny courtyard morning, {M2}.
M2
Cheerful is nice, {F3}, yet should a historic house not sound slower and more solemn?
M3
Solemn like a rainy Monday at the tax office, {M2}?
M2
Dignified! Majestic! Watch me set this old brass metronome to forty beats per minute!
F3
Listen to one bar at forty beats... tick... tock... everyone in {CITY} just fell asleep!
M3
Even the sparrows on the courtyard fountain stopped splashing and yawned, {M2}.
M2
Hmm, perhaps forty is slightly sleepy—what tempo wins a Golden Courtyard Plaque, {F3}?
F3
An honest tempo played from the heart, without peeking toward the street gate every bar.
M3
Besides, real judges notice whether the host looks relaxed and happy in his own house.
M2
Relaxed and happy! Right—I shall go relax vigorously at the front desk this instant!
F3
Take your brass metronome with you, {M2}, and breathe in four-quarter time!
scenes.outro: Rescued from forty-beat slumber, {F3} brings lively music back to Room 9 while {M3} heads down to the cellar workshop. See you next time.

scenes.title: Measuring the Cedar Frames
scenes.summary: On his lunch hour in the courtyard, M4 helps M3 measure four freestanding cedar-and-linen acoustic screens along the side brick arcade.
scenes.intro: At half past twelve in the sunny courtyard, {M4} walks over from City Hall carrying his wooden folding rule to help his younger brother {M3} measure the side brick wall. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M4
Show me where the sound bounced yesterday afternoon, little brother.
M3
Stand right beside the stone fountain and clap your hands once sharply, {M4}.
M4
Clap! Hear that quick metallic ring bouncing back off the bare brick arcade?
M3
Exactly—now hold this heavy folded linen tablecloth flat in front of the bricks.
M4
Clap! Whoa, the metallic ring vanished completely, and your voice sounds twice as warm!
M3
Four freestanding cedar frames, each one metre wide and two metres tall, wrapped in oatmeal linen.
M4
With wide oak feet at the bottom so not a single nail touches the historic brick!
M3
And {F2} suggested tucking small pots of fresh rosemary along the wooden bases.
M4
Good sound, good carpentry, AND good kitchen herbs—we can saw the cedar after five today!
M3
Did you hear anything more at City Hall about the Clock-Square display cabinet?
M4
Yes! While checking the archive register, I found a second entry about our gate plaque!
M3
Come tell {F1} inside—she has been waiting all morning for archive news!
scenes.outro: One clap beside a folded tablecloth proves {M3}'s acoustic design works—and {M4} brings fresh archive news from City Hall! See you next time.

scenes.title: Twin Plaques on One Street
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M4 shows F1 and M3 a historical street record proving the stonemason who built {SHOW} carved a pair of oval brass plaques on {STREET}.
scenes.intro: Inside at the quiet front desk, {M4} unfolds a photocopied archive sheet beside {F1} and {M3}. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
Look at that neat nineteenth-century handwriting—where did you find this page, {M4}?
M4
In the Municipal Street Builder Register for {STREET} across the square at City Hall!
M3
Read the line underlined near the bottom—there is our exact street number!
F1
Built around a central shade tree with an oval brass motto plaque beside the gate!
M4
Keep reading the next sentence, {F1}, because here is the surprise.
F1
Cast by the local foundry as a motto plaque rather than a simple house number!
M3
Wait—does the festival rulebook allow a motto plaque as our founding builder mark?
M4
Even better: the festival coordinator told me historic motto plaques earn bonus heritage credit!
F1
No wonder a velvet ribbon covered the bottom half inside that glass cabinet!
M3
Did the register record the exact words engraved on our oval plaque, {M4}?
M4
Only the foundry date—the motto itself we will read tomorrow when number ten unlocks it!
F1
Wait—look through the glass door: who is that quiet couple sketching our shade tree?!
scenes.outro: Our missing plaque holds a secret founding motto—and outside under the tree sits a quiet couple with a sketchbook! See you next time.

scenes.title: Two Quiet Guests Under the Tree
scenes.summary: While M2 naps briefly in his office, F1, F2, and M1 welcome a quiet couple under the courtyard tree with natural warmth and zero fuss.
scenes.intro: Out under the dappled shade of the courtyard tree, two polite afternoon visitors finish their tea and walk cheerfully out the gate as {F1}, {F2}, and {M1} clear the stoneware cups. Listen first.
story: F2
What a pleasant couple at table three—they asked all about our green sunroom shutters!
F1
And the lady noticed how level the third flagstone sits beside the tree trunk, {M1}!
M1
People who know stone joints always notice good sand bedding right away.
F2
Thank goodness {M2} went upstairs for ten minutes to hunt for his spare necktie!
F1
Otherwise he would have marched out in white cotton gloves with a brass metronome!
M1
Notice they paid full price in coins, left a neat tip, and asked zero fancy questions.
F2
True—probably just two retired teachers enjoying a sunny Tuesday walk down {STREET}.
F1
Still, treating every single neighbour and traveller warmly feels ten times easier than guessing!
M1
Write that rule on the wall, {F1}: good tea and clean stone need zero acting.
F2
Speaking of good tea, tomorrow morning I bake my brand-new festival signature pastry!
F1
Oooh, a brand-new creation for Saturday?! Tell us what goes inside, {F2}!
F2
Top secret until Wednesday noon—though {M1} had better sharpen his judging pencil!
scenes.outro: Natural warmth beats white gloves every time, and {F2} announces a mysterious new festival pastry for Wednesday! See you next time.

scenes.title: Ordering the Festival Sign
scenes.summary: Returning to the front desk with his glasses perched on his forehead, M2 proudly mails off an express order form for a modest cloth welcome sign.
scenes.intro: At four in the afternoon, {M2} strides briskly down the stairs waving a pink carbon-copy order form toward {F1} at the front desk. Listen first.
story: M2
Rejoice, {F1}! If Clock-Square Courtyard has glossy brochures, {SHOW} shall have a welcome sign!
F1
A neat painted wooden board beside the gate arch sounds lovely, {M2}!
M2
Even better: a washable cream cloth banner from the {CITY} Express Sign Workshop!
F1
Hold on—may I check the measurements on your pink carbon slip before it goes?
M2
Too late for bureaucracy—the express bicycle messenger rode off thirty seconds ago!
F1
{M2}... let me look at box three on your pink copy right here.
M2
Forty centimetres high by one hundred twenty centimetres wide—neat, modest, and dignified!
F1
Put your reading glasses on your nose and count the zeros in box three, {M2}.
M2
Glasses down... four... zero... zero?! FOUR HUNDRED CENTIMETRES WIDE BY TWO HUNDRED HIGH?!
F1
You ordered a FOUR-METRE cloth sail big enough to wrap a city bus!
M2
Call the sign shop! No, wait—express orders print immediately and have zero refunds!
F1
Brace yourself for Thursday delivery, boss—and look who just walked past our gate!
scenes.outro: One misplaced zero without reading glasses guarantees a four-metre surprise on Thursday—right as a familiar neighbour returns early! One more scene in Episode 2!

scenes.title: Number Ten Returns Early
scenes.summary: At sunset by the street gate, F3, M1, and F1 greet their violinist neighbour returning early from his trip—and he promises to unlock the archive display case at nine sharp Wednesday morning!
scenes.intro: Golden Tuesday sunset glows along {STREET} as {F3}, {M1}, and {F1} step out to water the gate flower pots—just as their violinist neighbour from house number ten walks up carrying a small travel bag. Listen first.
story: F3
Look who caught the early evening coach home—welcome back to {STREET}, my friend!
F1
Did he have a wonderful visit with his grandson, {F3}?
F3
He is smiling and nodding—and look, he heard we entered the Courtyard Festival!
M1
Ask him if he still keeps the brass key to that Clock-Square history cabinet, {F3}.
F3
Look at him patting his waistcoat pocket—he carries that archive key on his watch chain!
F1
NO WAY! Our founding oval brass plaque has been ten minutes away this whole time?!
M1
Tell him we have the original yellow polishing ticket and our blue-ink loan note.
F3
He remembers the day {M2} lent it ten summers ago—and says it belongs back home!
F1
When can we walk up to Clock-Square Pavilion together to unlock the glass case?!
F3
Nine sharp tomorrow morning, right after morning coffee!
M1
I will bring my brass polish cloth and four fresh bronze screws in my pocket.
F1
Tomorrow morning at nine, {SHOW} gets its history back!
scenes.outro: The archive key gleams on a neighbourly watch chain, setting up Wednesday morning's plaque rescue—and {F2}'s grand pastry unveiling! End of Episode 2—see you in Episode 3!
